name: Linear Depth Cueing via Fourier Projection-Slice Theorem
definition: A rendering technique that replaces per-voxel shading followed by projection with projection followed by per-pixel shading. It allows depth cueing (linear attenuation) to be computed efficiently by factoring the viewing direction out of the integral, resulting in four integrals evaluable via the Fourier projection-slice theorem.
summary: Linear Depth Cueing via Fourier Projection-Slice Theorem is a shading model that enhances depth perception in X-ray projections by efficiently computing linear attenuation through frequency-domain projection, avoiding occlusion.
